language.title: Language
language.lead: The whole site — chrome, help, print, and the assistant — follows this pick. Absent a pick, it follows the browser (French → français). Save settings to apply, or use the header control.

helpBody1: RE: tired projects a Canadian retirement drawdown year by year: growth while you contribute, then withdrawals across TFSA / taxable / RRSP-RRIF with federal and provincial tax, CPP, OAS (clawback + GIS) and RRIF minimums. Every input in the sidebar is documented on the Help page (top-right ? button), and the sections below let you edit the tax tables and engine assumptions themselves.
helpBody2: All profiles and settings are stored only in this browser's local storage — nothing is sent to a server. Use the sidebar's Export to back them up.
welcomeShow: Show the welcome section when the site loads
welcomeHint: The getting-started card reappears at the top of the main page on every visit. Dismissing it still hides it for the rest of the current session.
unsavedAsk: Ask before switching away from a scenario with unsaved edits
unsavedHint: When on, changing scenarios with unsaved edits asks whether to save first — with a "don't ask again" box that turns this off. Off = switch silently.
dangerBody: Erase it all: every scenario, engine setting, agent memory, AI chat, model connection, panel layout and dismissal is permanently deleted from this browser — including the database file itself — and the app restarts with factory defaults. Nothing is kept. Export a backup first if you might want any of it back.
invalid: Invalid configuration: check that every bracket has a rate (rates = brackets + 1) and all values are numbers.
resetConfirm: Reset all settings to the built-in defaults?
eraseConfirm1: Erase EVERYTHING — all scenarios, engine settings, agent memories, AI chats and model connections — from this browser? This cannot be undone.
eraseConfirm2: Really erase everything? Nothing is kept; the app restarts with factory defaults.

levers.title: Lever ranges
levers.lead: The sliders for spending, savings, expected return and volatility only span the range below. Widen one if your plan lives past the default edge — these are preferences, not engine settings, so they save the moment you change them. Retirement age, plan-to age, CPP and OAS start ages keep fixed spans; a fixed span is part of their meaning.

rrifLead: CRA minimum withdrawal rate by age (applied to the RRIF balance each year).

oas.gisCouple: GIS max annual — couple, per spouse ($/yr)
oas.gisReduction: GIS reduction rate (% per $ of non-OAS income)
oas.gisNote: With a spouse enabled, each spouse's GIS is assessed on combined non-OAS income at the couple rate when both receive OAS (single rate when only one does) — CRA's couple rules.

cpp.selfEmployedLead: Self-employed CPP contribution (both sides) — a deduction from taxable self-employment income.

gains.acb: Taxable account starting ACB (% of balance)
gains.note: 100% = the whole taxable balance is principal (no embedded gains). Lower it if the account has grown — e.g. 60% means 40¢ of every dollar withdrawn is a taxable gain. Contributions raise the ACB; growth does not.

rdsp.lead: Canada Disability Savings Grant (CDSG) matches contributions; the Bond (CDSB) is income-tested and needs no contribution. Both stop at the end-age; contributions have a lifetime cap. On withdrawal the grant/bond/growth portion is taxable. 2026 values.
rdsp.note: Family income at/below the grant threshold earns 300% on the first $500 + 200% on the next $1,000 contributed; above it, 100% on the first $1,000. The bond pays in full at/below the lower threshold, phases out linearly to $0 at the upper. The 10-year AHA clawback and the grant/bond carry-forward are not modelled.

fhsa.note: FHSA contributions are deductible (like an RRSP), grow tax-sheltered, and are capped by the annual and lifetime limits. The plan can stay open for a limited number of years from when it was opened. On retirement the balance transfers to the RRSP (no RRSP room needed). A qualifying first-home withdrawal (tax-free) is not modelled.

engine.roomNote: Used only when a scenario tracks contribution room (TFSA/RRSP room set on the sidebar). Each year TFSA room grows by this limit; RRSP room grows by 18% of earned income up to this maximum (minus any pension adjustment). When "Index tax tables" is on, both grow with CPI like the real CRA limits.
engine.pensionSplitNote: Couples only: up to this share of each spouse's eligible pension income (RRIF/RRSP draws and DB pensions — not CPP/OAS) is reallocated to the lower-taxed spouse to cut household tax. CRA's maximum is 50%; set 0 to disable. Only reported tax changes — GIS and the withdrawal plan are unaffected.
engine.growSpend: Grow spending with inflation each year
engine.growSpendHint: On: the Spending Target column rises with CPI — a $60k lifestyle entered today needs ~$89k of income 20 years out at 2%. Off: the target stays flat in today's dollars (a level-spending / real-terms plan).
engine.indexTax: Index tax tables, OAS and CPP to inflation each year
engine.indexTaxHint: Brackets, basic personal amounts, the OAS clawback threshold and benefit amounts all grow with CPI — closer to reality (CRA indexes them), but results are then in inflated future dollars.
engine.togglesNote: These two toggles are independent. Grow spending controls whether your spending target inflates; Index tax tables controls whether the tax system and benefits inflate. The CPI rate above drives both. For a fully "today's dollars" (real-terms) plan, turn spending growth off; for nominal, leave it on.

assistant.whatIsSentLead: Every request to the model is assembled from the pieces below. Uncheck one to drop it. Edits save immediately (same as lever ranges) and apply to the next message in every chat. Per-chat notes still live on the composer.
assistant.assembledLead: Exactly what the next message will put in the system slot. Empty means nothing — no blank system role, and the local engine drops its previous system from cache. Chat history still goes as user/assistant turns.
assistant.toolsPerModelLead: The catalog decides the default: Qwen 1.7B and Bonsai 1.7B are questions-only; 4B and up run tools. Force a model on or off here for testing — Auto restores the catalog. Cloud models always use tools unless Send tools is unchecked above.
assistant.personaHint: Replaces the built-in planner voice when non-empty. Leave blank to use the default.
assistant.toolNativeHint: How a function-calling model should use the tools. Sent only when Tool instructions is on and the model is cloud.
assistant.toolPromptHint: How a chat-only local model should use TOOL_CALL. The catalog of tools is a separate toggle.
assistant.toolOffHint: Used when this model's tools are off (catalog default or your override), or when Send tools is unchecked.

includePersona.label: Persona
includePersona.hint: The base voice (built-in or your override).

includePageLine.label: Current page
includePageLine.hint: One line naming the page you are on.

includeToolInstructions.label: Tool instructions
includeToolInstructions.hint: How to use tools / what to do when tools are off.

includePromptCatalog.label: Tool catalog (local)
includePromptCatalog.hint: The TOOL_CALL: list of every tool. Local models only.

includeProgramRules.label: Program rules
includeProgramRules.hint: Live CPP/OAS/GIS/RRIF/limit figures from engine settings.

includePlanDigest.label: Plan digest (local)
includePlanDigest.hint: Pinned summary of ages, balances, projection. Local models only.

includeChatNote.label: Per-chat note
includeChatNote.hint: “Additional instructions for this chat” from the composer.

sendTools.label: Send tools
sendTools.hint: Advertise and execute tools. Off = chat only, even on a capable model.

personaLast.label: Persona last
personaLast.hint: Put the persona after the mechanics so a small model honors a custom override.
